records.name: Cars
records.summary: Electric models accounted for one-quarter of new car sales worldwide in 2025.
records.scope: New sales, not the share of cars already on the road. IEA electric-car figures include battery electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles.

reference.name: IEA · Global EV Outlook 2026: Executive summary

records.name: Trucks
records.measure: Electric share of new truck sales
records.summary: Electric truck sales exceeded 400,000; battery electric models made up 97% of electric truck sales.
records.scope: Medium and heavy freight trucks. This is a sales share, not a fleet share.

reference.name: IEA · Global EV Outlook 2026: Other EV modes

records.name: Buses
records.summary: Electric bus sales grew 12% in 2025. Battery electric models represented 98% of electric bus sales.
records.scope: Buses with at least 10 seats, including urban and intercity services. Not a city-bus-only measure.

reference.name: IEA · Global EV Outlook 2026: Other EV modes

records.name: Motor Bikes
records.measure: Electric share of new two-wheeler sales
records.summary: Almost 10 million electric two-wheelers were sold globally in 2025.
records.scope: IEA two-wheelers include motorcycles and mopeds with a top speed of at least 25 km/h. Excludes electric-assisted bicycles and low-speed scooters; not a motorcycle-only measure.

reference.name: IEA · Global EV Outlook 2026: Other EV modes

records.name: Trains
records.measure: Passenger rail activity on electric trains
records.summary: The IEA’s 2019 rail report describes roughly three-quarters of passenger rail activity as electric, using historical data through 2016.
records.scope: Historical passenger transport activity, not the share of locomotives or track electrified. Includes externally supplied electricity; this is not a battery-train statistic.

records.name: Boats
records.summary: EMSA identifies ferries and short voyages as key battery applications. Battery energy density limits longer autonomous voyages.
records.scope: Qualitative guidance, not a measured adoption rate. Pure electric, hybrid and plug-in hybrid vessels differ; shore power alone does not imply electric propulsion.

reference.name: EMSA · Ship electrification
reference.coverage: Maritime technology guidance · no global fleet series

records.title: Start of the Holocene Epoch
records.description: Retreat of continental ice sheets and emergence of early human agriculture and settlements.

records.title: Mid-Holocene Climate Optimum
records.description: Warm, stable global climate supporting early agricultural societies in Mesopotamia, the Nile, and Indus valleys.

records.title: Egyptian Old Kingdom & Bronze Age
records.description: Pyramids of Giza constructed; atmospheric CO2 remains strictly locked between 260 and 270 ppm.

records.title: Common Era / Roman Empire
records.description: Peak Roman and Han Dynasty agricultural land use; stable atmospheric baseline continues.

records.title: Onset of Industrial Revolution
records.description: Invention of James Watt's steam engine; beginning of coal-powered mechanization in Britain.

records.title: Official IPCC Benchmark (1850–1900)
records.description: Global industrialization gathers pace. Pre-industrial atmospheric benchmark conventionally set at ~280 ppm.

records.title: Keeling Curve Initiated
records.description: Dr. Charles David Keeling begins continuous in-situ atmospheric monitoring at NOAA Mauna Loa Observatory, Hawaii.

records.title: Breaching 400 ppm Threshold
records.description: Daily Mauna Loa CO2 readings permanently cross 400 ppm for the first time in over 3 million years (Pliocene epoch).

records.title: Present Day Atmospheric Peak
records.description: Global annual mean exceeds 426 ppm (427.35 ppm NOAA Mauna Loa), +52% above the 10,000-year Holocene baseline.

records.title: 1950s Southwest & Southern Plains Aridity
records.description: Post-WWII prolonged dry spell affecting California, Nevada, and the Southwest with repeated seasonal deficits.

records.title: Historic Northeast Drought of the 1960s
records.description: Severe multi-year drought across New England, New York, and the Mid-Atlantic. Reservoir levels fell to historic lows, triggering regional emergency rationing.

records.title: 1976–1977 California Severe Drought Crisis
records.description: One of the sharpest 2-year precipitation deficits in modern West Coast history. Snowpacks virtually disappeared, sparking modern statewide water management reforms.

records.title: 1982–1983 Super El Niño Moisture Surplus
records.description: Intense atmospheric rivers dumped unprecedented rain and snow across California and Nevada, producing the highest wet index anomaly (+4.88) in the 76-year record.

records.title: 1987–1992 Six-Year Western Drought
records.description: Six consecutive dry years in California depleted state reservoirs to 32% of capacity, accelerating groundwater overdraft across the Central Valley.

records.title: 2012–2016 Exceptional California Megadrought
records.description: Record-high temperatures exacerbated precipitation deficits, creating a "hot drought." Governor Brown declared a statewide state of emergency with mandatory 25% urban reductions.

records.title: 2020–2022 Western North America Megadrought Peak
records.description: Tree-ring studies confirmed 2000–2022 was the driest 22-year period in southwestern North America since at least 800 CE. Lake Mead and Lake Powell dropped to record crisis levels.

records.title: 2024–2025 Trans-Continental Regional Divergence
records.description: While California experienced atmospheric river recovery in 2023, the Northeast plunged into an unexpected severe flash drought in late 2024–2025 (-3.22 PDSI).

records.title: Peak Fire Frequency (9,719 Fires)
records.description: Highest total count of ignitions in the 21st century dataset, but moderate acreage burned.

records.title: Northwest Territories Extreme Season
records.description: Massive boreal forest fires in the subarctic burning over 11 million acres.

records.title: Fort McMurray Horse River Megafire
records.description: Destructive urban-wildland interface blaze forcing the evacuation of 88,000 residents in Alberta.

records.title: Unprecedented Historic Record (43.51M Acres)
records.description: The most catastrophic wildfire season in modern Canadian history. More than double previous records; smoke blanketed eastern North America and crossed the Atlantic.

records.title: Second Most Severe Season (21.25M Acres)
records.description: Continued megafire conditions across British Columbia, Alberta, and the Northwest Territories.

records.title: 2026 Season (As of Sept 2026)
records.description: Year-to-date data as of September 2026 indicates continued elevated fire activity (11.20 million acres burned across 5,248 fires).

records.title: Mid-20th Century Baseline: 0.5 High-Tide Flood Days/Yr
records.description: Sunny-day high tide coastal flooding was rare (< 1 day per year national median). EM-DAT recorded approximately 15 major flood disasters globally per year.

records.title: 1982–1983 Super El Niño Pacific Coastal Surges
records.description: Unprecedented atmospheric rivers dumped record precipitation while high astronomical tides battered the Pacific coastline, prompting nationwide coastal levee and revetment overhauls.

records.title: The Great Midwest Flood of 1993 (~$44B)
records.description: Persistent downpours inundated 9 Midwestern states for months. Hundreds of levees failed, submerging 20 million acres and driving 1990s inland flood losses to $62.4B.

records.title: Hurricane Katrina Storm Surge Catastrophe ($200B+)
records.description: A 28-foot storm surge overwhelmed federal levee defenses, submerging 80% of New Orleans and propelling 2000s tropical cyclone losses to an unprecedented $436.0B.

records.title: Superstorm Sandy Record Metro Surge ($90B+)
records.description: A 14-foot storm surge hit at astronomical high tide, inundating Manhattan subway tunnels and coastal communities, laying bare the risk of baseline sea level rise.

records.title: Hurricane Harvey 60-Inch Cloudburst ($160B+)
records.description: Stalled tropical system dropped over 60 inches of rain across Greater Houston, an extreme downpour volume directly turbocharged by atmospheric warming (+7% water vapor capacity per 1°C).

records.title: Hurricane Ida Compound Surge & Flash Flood ($85B+)
records.description: Category 4 storm surged through Louisiana before remnant cloudbursts dumped 3.15 inches of rain in a single hour in NYC, inundating subways and urban highway networks.

records.title: Hurricane Helene Southern Appalachian Inundation ($50B+)
records.description: Atmospheric moisture combined with mountainous terrain to drop 30+ inches of rain into river valleys, causing catastrophic flash flooding hundreds of miles inland.

records.title: Sunny-Day Nuisance Flooding Reaches 5.0 Days/Year
records.description: NOAA confirms national median high-tide flood frequency reached 5.0 days/year (a 10-fold surge since 1950). Southeast Atlantic and Gulf cities experience 400% to 1,100% increases since 2000 with no storm present.
